findings.reason: node (d) would be built to compute the wrong statistic, and §2's re-measure, the stated purpose of §9(d) ("the recurrence §2's re-measure needs"), would be invalid without either adding the acted-on filter to the fold or restating which baseline it compares against.
findings.text: §9(d) defines the fold as "the share of findings that follow an earlier review of the same plan raising the same type", which is §1's same-type recurrence (that review measured "83% of `duplicate_owner` findings follow a review that raised the same type", line 63, and the retention decision calls it "the 83% same-type recurrence", line 131), yet §9(d) asserts "That is the figure §2's one-week re-measure compares against 41.9%"; §2's baseline is a different denominator — the recurrence "after an **acted** same-type finding … the 41.9% baseline for `duplicate_owner`" (line 70 as collapsed; the pre-collapse §2 done-when states the acted qualifier, recovered from commit 76ceee424). A fold that never checks whether the earlier same-type finding was answered/acted on reproduces the 83% figure, not the 41.9% one, so §2's re-measure would compare a raised-based share against an acted-based baseline

findings.reason: per the plan's own convention (each §8 node and §4 node declared and recorded a red control; the §4 done-when finding was declined on exactly that ground), three of §9's four nodes cannot show their guard fires, so their gates would pass on unfixed code and the plan should either add a declared control per node or say why none applies.
findings.text: §9's nodes (a), (b) and (d) state a done-when but name no declared negative control: (a) says "the fork is gone, and a test shows `read_blobs` returning a bare blob's bytes and `None` for a missing one", (b) says "no caller-unread value remains, checked by a search the node runs", and (d) says a fixture "gives the expected share per type", none stating the mutation must fail — while (c) does declare one ("the new test fails when the content branch's hot guard is removed"
